heroHeadline: Day 612: Sheinbaum Launches 93B-Peso Petrochemical Plan from Minatitlán; CNTE Strike Day 5 as World Cup Opener Approaches June 11; Ley Monreal Now Law After Judicial Decrees Enter Force June 3
heroSubtitle: June 5, 2026 marks Day 612 of Claudia Sheinbaum's presidency. Sheinbaum held her mañanera from Minatitlán, Veracruz, launching a 93-billion-peso strategic investment plan for the petrochemical and fertilizer sector (2026–2030), aligned with the Pemex-Petrobras deepwater collaboration agreement announced June 2. The CNTE national teachers' strike entered its fifth consecutive day with over 2 million students affected across 29 states and no agreement in sight — Sheinbaum has declined a direct meeting with CNTE leadership, leaving SEGOB (Rosa Icela Rodríguez) and SEP (Mario Delgado) to manage dialogue. The World Cup opener (Mexico vs. South Africa, Estadio Azteca) is six days away. Key developments this week: (June 2) Sheinbaum publicly rebuked U.S. Ambassador Ronald Johnson at the mañanera — 'The ambassador should respect Mexico's internal affairs' — after he criticized her sovereignty rally on social media; Pemex-Petrobras deepwater deal imminent. (June 3) Three judicial and electoral reform decrees entered into force: judicial elections postponed to 2028, 'Ley Monreal' on foreign electoral interference now law, INE integrity commission operational; CNTE stormed SEP headquarters and blocked Reforma for 4 hours; USMCA Round 2 confirmed for June 16–17 in Washington with ~85% of USMCA exports expected exempt from U.S. forced-labor tariffs. (June 4) Sheinbaum signed the National Tomato Price Agreement to reduce food costs; defended AMLO's letter to Trump at the mañanera. Iran's national team confirmed arrived in Tijuana for World Cup base camp on June 5.
